text: Use when a compiled scene has a preflight, visual or request-satisfaction defect, or an existing design needs a scoped edit.
note: Covers follow-up edits too, so it competes with the system prompt's follow-up routine.

text: Read the actual current diagnostics/critique and inspect the implicated geometry. Change the smallest coherent part that fully fixes the failure; recompose that part when tiny adjustments cannot solve the reading order or density.
Preserve successful unrelated content and the user's chosen sources.
note: Keep-it rule #5 (same words as A1 step 2).

text: Anchor the repair to the current saved scene, not a remembered template. Separate the properties the user wants changed from those already approved. A spacing repair … must not silently rebind a typography role, reset a corner radius or restyle a neighboring component.

Inspect existing bindings and effective values before editing. Prefer property-level modify operations when the structure is already sound. Reapplying style($type.<role>) can change several effective fields at once.
If a subtree really needs reconciliation, retain its unrelated existing fields and compare them with the saved baseline afterward.

For a requested color match, inspect the actual target and current rendered colors using the scene and pinned kit's active mode. A token named cream, accent or primary is not evidence of its appearance … Keeping the same rejected value and describing it differently is not a repair. If the target is unavailable, name the gap.
This does not authorize recoloring authentic logo/product pixels or changing the workspace's Brand Kit globally. brand-and-tokens owns palette selection.

When moving support closer to a headline, inspect measured text lines and reflow dependent positions … Preserve the approved headline treatment; assess both optical grouping and comfortable type size … A narrower gap alone does not rescue unreadable text.
Use compile_dsl_block with modify lines for properties or reconcile for a container's intended subtree. Do not re-declare an existing page; page edits use #page:<id>.
note: Conflicts with the follow-up routine (A1): "Make the change with apply_structured_edit … compile_dsl_block only when the change needs new structure". This skill never mentions apply_structured_edit.

text: Omitted human content is protected; deleting it requires an explicit directive.
Keep the shared creative direction current when copy, evidence or source choices change; validate the revised record with its revision reason before using it.
note: Conflicts with the follow-up routine: "do not rewrite or re-validate creative-direction.json".

text: Record the repair delta once in the active round, then preflight, render and view the new scene. Check the requested change and preserved properties against the baseline; disclose any remaining mismatch … An old acceptance cannot certify a repaired artifact.
note: Conflicts with the follow-up routine: "Do not write critique.json or round notes".
